title: Define and Limit the Purpose
where_to_look: Review the preamble or recitals, Purpose or Project definition, and Confidential Information use limitation.
required: Require a completed, deal-specific Purpose identifying the project, products, services, or transaction, with disclosure and use limited to that Purpose.
fallback: Accept a defined business-relationship Purpose without further detail only if disclosure and use remain limited to that Purpose and no open-ended fallback applies.
escalate_if: Escalate any blank or placeholder Purpose, fallback to actual cooperation or future business, or use language reaching beyond the stated Purpose.
flag_if: The Purpose is blank, bracketed, or a template placeholder.
The Purpose is defined as actual cooperation, ongoing business, or any future relationship.
Confidential Information is not expressly limited to information related to the Purpose, Project, or Transaction.
Permitted use extends to activities or business opportunities outside the stated Purpose.
Affiliates or later agreements are included without identifying their connection to the Purpose.
preferred_language: The parties may disclose Confidential Information solely to evaluate and pursue [the specific project, transaction, products, services, or business relationship] and related discussions and activities expressly contemplated by that purpose (the “Purpose”). Confidential Information means non-public information disclosed by either party that relates to the Purpose. Neither party may use Confidential Information for any other project, transaction, product, service, or business activity.
confidence_note: Based on 355 findings across numerous counterparties, direction is highly consistent on completing and defining the Purpose and linking covered information to it, while transaction detail varies by deal.

title: Confidential-information definition and scope
where_to_look: The definitions section, including the Confidential Information exclusions and designation provisions.
required: Require a mutual, non-exclusive definition of non-public, Purpose-related information in any form, including unmarked observations.
fallback: Accept a definition limited to non-public, Purpose-related information in all media, with a reasonable-person catchall for unmarked material.
escalate_if: Escalate any definition that covers public or unrelated information or makes marking and written confirmation the sole path to protection.
flag_if: The definition covers all information without a non-public qualifier.
The definition omits a link to the Purpose, Transaction, or Relationship.
The clause makes marking or written confirmation the sole route to protect oral or visual information.
The definition omits information learned by observation or inspection.
The examples are exhaustive rather than illustrative.
preferred_language: “Confidential Information” means all non-public information related to the Purpose disclosed or made available by or on behalf of a Disclosing Party to a Receiving Party in any form or medium, including written, oral, visual, electronic, or tangible form and information learned by observation or inspection. The listed categories are illustrative and not exhaustive. Information is Confidential Information whether or not marked or identified as confidential if a reasonable person would understand it to be confidential from its nature or the circumstances of disclosure.
confidence_note: Based on 1,603 findings across a broad contract set, the direction is highly consistent, with repeated high-significance moves toward bounded scope and protection for unmarked and observed information.

title: Preserve standard confidentiality exclusions
where_to_look: Review the Confidential Information definition and its exclusions or exceptions subsection.
required: Require exclusions for prior possession, later public availability, lawful third-party receipt, and independent development by or for Recipient without use or reference.
fallback: Accept development by Recipient rather than by or for Recipient only if the other exclusions and no-use/no-reference test remain.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that removes the core exclusions, imposes clear-and-convincing proof, or protects Recipient-caused breaches.
flag_if: The exclusions omit prior knowledge or prior possession.
The public-domain exclusion omits information that later becomes public.
The third-party-source exclusion lacks a Recipient knowledge qualifier.
The independent-development exclusion omits work performed for Recipient.
The independent-development exclusion lacks a no-use and no-reference requirement.
preferred_language: Confidential Information does not include information already known to or possessed by Recipient at the time of disclosure, information that is or becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this Agreement by Recipient or its Representatives, information lawfully received from a third party that, to Recipient’s reasonable knowledge, had the right to disclose it, or information independently developed by or for Recipient without use of or reference to Discloser’s Confidential Information.

title: Purpose-Limited Use and Necessary Copying
where_to_look: Use restrictions, copying provisions, and confidentiality-handling obligations.
required: Require use solely for the defined Purpose and copying only as necessary, with all copies marked and protected like originals.
fallback: Accept Purpose-related copying and use under a later written agreement between the parties, with equivalent safeguards and consent for other uses.
escalate_if: Escalate if the clause permits unrestricted non-Purpose use, copying, technical extraction, derivative development, or AI training.
flag_if: The permitted-use language authorizes use for any purpose beyond the defined Purpose.
The copying restriction lacks a necessity, minimum-extent, or prior-consent limitation.
Copies need not retain the original confidentiality markings or remain subject to the agreement.
The clause permits reverse engineering, decompilation, disassembly, or derivative development.
The clause permits use in artificial intelligence, machine learning, analytics, or algorithm training.
preferred_language: The Receiving Party shall use the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information solely for the Purpose and only to the extent necessary to carry out the Purpose. The Receiving Party may copy or reproduce Confidential Information only to the minimum extent necessary for the Purpose. Each copy shall retain all confidentiality or proprietary legends on the original and shall remain subject to this Agreement. Except as expressly permitted by this Agreement, the Receiving Party shall not otherwise use, copy, reproduce, modify, reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, derive from, or disclose Confidential Information without the Disclosing Party’s prior written consent.
confidence_note: Based on 348 findings across numerous counterparties, the direction is strong and consistent on Purpose-limited use and necessary copying, with mixed treatment of subsequent agreements and specialized prohibitions.

title: Compelled and Legally Required Disclosure Procedures
where_to_look: Required disclosure, legal-process, subpoena, court-order, or governmental-disclosure provisions.
required: Require legally permissible prompt notice, Discloser-funded protective relief, minimum necessary disclosure, and confidential-treatment assurances.
fallback: Accept reasonable-efforts language and no express cost allocation only if minimum disclosure and confidential-treatment assurances remain.
escalate_if: Never accept language permitting compelled production beyond what counsel advises is required without attorney review.
flag_if: The clause imposes notice without a legally permissible qualifier.
The clause omits an opportunity to seek protective relief or waive compliance.
The clause lacks a minimum-disclosure limit tied to counsel’s advice.
The clause lacks a duty to seek reliable assurances of confidential treatment.
The clause makes the Recipient pay for the Disclosing Party’s protective efforts.
preferred_language: If Recipient is required by law, regulation, court order, subpoena, or other compulsory legal process to disclose Confidential Information, Recipient shall, to the extent legally permissible, promptly notify Disclosing Party in writing before disclosure so Disclosing Party, at its sole expense, may seek a protective order or other remedy or waive compliance; absent a protective order, other remedy, or waiver, Recipient shall disclose only the portion of Confidential Information and only to the persons its counsel advises it must provide, and shall seek reliable assurances that the disclosure will receive confidential treatment.
confidence_note: Based on 1,301 findings across a broad set of counterparties, the direction is highly consistent toward legally permissible notice, Discloser-funded protection, minimum disclosure, and confidential-treatment assurances.

title: Defined term and mutual convenience termination
where_to_look: Term, Termination, Duration, Expiration, and Survival provisions.
required: Require a defined term of no more than two years, mutual 30-day convenience termination, and express confidentiality survival.
fallback: Accept a three-year defined term with mutual 30-day convenience termination and confidentiality survival, including trade-secret protection.
escalate_if: Escalate any indefinite or relationship-based term, one-sided termination right, or survival gap to an attorney.
flag_if: The Agreement has no stated expiration date.
The term is tied only to the parties’ relationship or ongoing discussions.
The stated term exceeds two years.
Only one party may terminate for convenience.
Confidentiality obligations do not expressly survive termination or expiration.
preferred_language: Term. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall expire two (2) years thereafter unless either Party terminates it earlier for convenience upon thirty (30) days’ written notice to the other Party. Termination or expiration shall not affect confidentiality obligations for Confidential Information disclosed before termination or expiration. Those obligations shall survive for five (5) years after termination or expiration, and trade-secret information shall remain protected for so long as it qualifies as a trade secret.
confidence_note: Based on 619 findings across numerous counterparties, the direction is highly consistent toward a defined one- to three-year term, bilateral notice termination, and continued confidentiality protection.

title: NDA Return, Destruction, and Backup Retention
where_to_look: Return or destruction, retained copies, backup systems, and survival provisions.
required: Require a one-copy right covering Confidential Information and derivatives for legal, regulatory, compliance, or document-retention purposes, plus a non-segregable routine-backup carve-out.
fallback: Accept a narrower right for one legally mandated or dispute-resolution copy and ordinary-course backups, provided confidentiality continues through retention and backups are later deleted in the ordinary course.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that permits unrestricted retention or use, or ends confidentiality before retained information is destroyed.
flag_if: Return or destruction is required immediately upon termination or request with no retention exception.
Retention is limited to a single memorial copy of the agreement rather than Confidential Information.
Routine disaster-recovery or automatically archived backup copies are subject to immediate deletion.
Confidentiality does not expressly continue for the entire retention period.
Derivative materials are omitted from the retention carve-out.
preferred_language: Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Receiving Party may retain one copy of Confidential Information and anything deriving therefrom for legal, regulatory, compliance, or document-retention purposes. The Receiving Party need not return or destroy Confidential Information or anything deriving therefrom that is not reasonably capable of being readily located or segregated, including routine disaster-backup media, provided that all retained information remains confidential and subject to this Agreement for the period of retention and is destroyed in the ordinary course of business.
confidence_note: Based on 1,334 findings across many counterparties, with highly consistent direction toward one-copy and routine-backup retention subject to continuing confidentiality.

title: Confidentiality Survival and Protected-Information Extensions
where_to_look: Term, termination, confidentiality-period, restricted-period, and survival provisions.
required: Require a fixed five-year period for ordinary Confidential Information, with trade secrets protected while legally qualifying and Personal Information protected for the longer of five years or the period required by law.
fallback: Accept a three-year period for ordinary Confidential Information if termination and expiration are covered and the trade-secret and legally required Personal Information extensions remain.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that makes ordinary Confidential Information perpetual or omits applicable-law protection for trade secrets or Personal Information.
flag_if: The clause does not expressly survive both termination and expiration.
The ordinary confidentiality period is perpetual or lacks a fixed end date.
The clause lacks protection for trade secrets while they qualify under applicable law.
Personal Information is not protected for the period required by applicable law.
The stated ordinary period is shorter than three years.
preferred_language: The confidentiality, non-use, and non-disclosure obligations shall survive termination or expiration of this Agreement for five (5) years following the later of the date of the last disclosure of Confidential Information and the date of termination or expiration; provided that Confidential Information that qualifies as a trade secret under applicable law shall remain confidential and subject to the applicable non-use restrictions for so long as it so qualifies, and Personal Information shall remain protected for the longer of five (5) years or the period required by applicable law.
confidence_note: Based on 912 findings, the pattern is highly consistent and predominantly high-significance for finite ordinary periods with trade-secret extensions; Personal Information extensions appear in fewer and more mixed findings.

title: Governing law: fixed Delaware substantive law
where_to_look: Governing law, applicable law, choice-of-law, or controlling-law clause.
required: Require Delaware substantive and internal law, expressly excluding conflicts-of-law rules.
fallback: Accept a fixed, mutually acceptable U.S. state governing law that applies substantive law and excludes conflicts-of-law rules.
escalate_if: Escalate before accepting foreign law, variable or domicile-based law, or any clause allowing conflicts rules to select another law.
flag_if: The clause names a foreign jurisdiction as governing law.
The clause ties governing law to a party’s location, domicile, office, or incorporation.
The clause omits an express exclusion of conflicts-of-law rules.
The clause selects governing law different from the forum law.
The clause contains inconsistent state references or unresolved placeholders.
preferred_language: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the internal substantive laws of the State of Delaware, without giving effect to any choice-of-law or conflict-of-law provision or rule that would cause the laws of any other jurisdiction to apply.
confidence_note: Based on 839 findings, the direction is overwhelmingly consistent toward fixed U.S. governing law, especially Delaware, with frequent conflicts-of-law exclusions.

title: Equitable and Injunctive Remedies
where_to_look: Remedies, equitable-relief, injunctive-relief, and specific-performance clauses.
required: Require the non-breaching party to have an express right to seek injunctive relief, specific performance, and other equitable relief for actual or threatened breach without bond or security.
fallback: Accept an express, court-discretionary right to seek injunctive or other equitable relief for actual or threatened breach, even if specific performance or the no-bond waiver is omitted.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that guarantees issuance of relief, requires advance consent to an injunction, or bars the receiving party from contesting adequacy of legal remedies.
flag_if: The clause states that a breach will cause irreparable harm or that no adequate remedy at law exists.
The clause states that a party may obtain relief or consents to entry of an injunction.
The clause waives or prohibits the adequate-remedy-at-law defense.
The clause covers only an actual breach and omits threatened breaches.
The clause makes injunctive relief conditional on posting bond or other security.
preferred_language: The parties acknowledge that an actual or threatened breach may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages may not be adequate. The non-breaching Party may seek, in any court of competent jurisdiction, temporary, preliminary, or permanent injunctive relief, specific performance, and other equitable relief without posting bond or other security. These remedies are cumulative and non-exclusive, and issuance remains subject to the court’s determination.
confidence_note: Based on 840 findings, the pattern is highly consistent and high-stakes: preserve express seek-based equitable relief, soften categorical harm admissions, and waive bond requirements, while treatment of damages-proof waivers is mixed.

title: Complete and Consistent Party Identification and Execution
where_to_look: Preamble, party-identification definitions, notices, signature blocks, and effective-date or execution provisions.
required: Require each party’s full legal name, entity details, and address in the preamble, with matching names and complete execution details in every signature block.
fallback: Accept defined short names and a separate notice address, but require the full legal entity name and matching entity name in the final signature block.
escalate_if: Never accept a mismatch in legal entity, entity form, jurisdiction, or execution date, or a signature by an affiliate or unauthorized representative, without an attorney.
flag_if: A party name is blank or bracketed in the preamble.
A signature block uses a generic party label.
A party name differs between the preamble and signature block.
The entity type or jurisdiction is missing or inconsistent.
The effective date or signature date is blank or inconsistent.
preferred_language: Each party shall be identified in this Agreement by its full legal name, entity type, jurisdiction of formation, and address, and may thereafter be referred to by a defined short name; each party shall execute this Agreement in that same legal name through an authorized representative whose name, title, signature, and date appear in the applicable signature block; and this Agreement shall be effective on the date of the last signature below.
confidence_note: Based on 1,256 total findings, the pattern is overwhelmingly consistent and predominantly high-significance, with repeated corrections to party identity, entity details, signature blocks, and execution dates.

title: Assignment, Transfer, Successors, and Change of Control
where_to_look: Assignment, transfer, successors-and-assigns, delegation, and change-of-control provisions.
required: Require mutual consent for ordinary assignments, with consent not unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and reciprocal corporate-transaction exceptions.
fallback: Accept reciprocal consent language with mutual affiliate and corporate-transaction exceptions, written notice, successor assumption, and continuing assignor liability.
escalate_if: Escalate if ordinary third-party transfers lack consent or notice, or if a transfer does not require successor assumption.
flag_if: The assignment restriction is unilateral rather than mutual.
Consent may be withheld or delayed in sole or absolute discretion.
The clause contains a one-sided affiliate, successor, or corporate-transaction exception.
The clause omits change of control or operation-of-law transfers from the restriction.
The assignor is released from obligations or the successor need not assume them.
preferred_language: Neither Party may assign, transfer, delegate, or otherwise dispose of this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of the non-assigning Party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided that either Party may assign this Agreement without consent to an Affiliate or to a successor or acquirer in connection with a merger, reorganization, change of control, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, upon written notice, if the assignee assumes this Agreement in writing and the assigning Party remains liable for obligations accrued before the assignment. This Agreement binds permitted successors and assigns.
confidence_note: Based on 844 findings across many counterparties, the direction is highly consistent, with predominantly medium-significance edits and recurring high-significance mutuality and corporate-transaction changes.
